package_info.why_malicious: These versions of the Spring Framework contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (Spring4Shell) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code under specific deployment conditions, potentially leading to full system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: spring-beans (invoked via spring-webmvc or spring-webflux dependency in a WAR deployment on Tomcat, JDK 9+)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: No explicit code snippet provided in the report, but the vulnerability is due to unsafe data binding in the Spring Framework, allowing attackers to craft HTTP requests that manipulate class loader properties and write arbitrary files (such as web shells) to the server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes specially crafted HTTP requests that exploit unsafe data binding, allowing attackers to set class loader properties and write arbitrary files to the web root, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to manipulate internal framework properties and write files to arbitrary locations via HTTP requests is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal data binding should only map safe, expected user input to application objects, not allow modification of class loader or file system properties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve safe, restricted data binding for form input, not arbitrary property manipulation.
key_indicators: Ability to set arbitrary properties via HTTP parameters
Writing files to web root or arbitrary locations
Triggering code execution through uploaded web shells

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to the vulnerable Spring application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Manipulation of internal class loader properties and file paths.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable data binding mechanism processes the request, allowing attacker-controlled values to be set.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary file write (e.g., web shell) to the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses the uploaded web shell or malicious file to execute arbitrary commands on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and potential full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests containing class loader or file path parameters
Unexpected file creation in web root or application directories
Execution of new files (e.g., web shells) shortly after suspicious HTTP requests
file_indicators: Unexpected .jsp, .war, or executable files in web root
Files with names or content not matching normal deployment artifacts
network_indicators: Unusual HTTP POST/GET requests with property manipulation parameters
Outbound connections initiated by newly created web shells
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP requests containing suspicious parameters that attempt to set class loader or file path properties. Watch for new files appearing in the web root or application directories, especially .jsp or .war files. Correlate these events with subsequent command execution or outbound network activity. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) with rules targeting known Spring4Shell exploit patterns.
